_doc: Findings ('what the data shows') contract. Rendered by harness/build_essays.py into <section id='findings'>. {{fact:KEY}} tokens are replaced at build time with live figures from harness/findings_facts.compute_facts(), so this prose stays true to the current data. Methodology: contract/findings_writing.json. {{cite:KEY}} resolve to numbered footnotes.

blocks.text: The index scores {{fact:total}} entities across {{fact:n_layers}} layers — {{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs and brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} in the tail — while live registers still load. Only {{fact:measured_pct}} of the weight rests on measured evidence, so what follows is a provisional read of structure, not a published pecking order. The point is not yet the magnitudes. It is that the shape the model was built to detect is already legible in the scatter before every sub-factor firms up.
The scatter is the argument made visible — each dot is one entity on axes the market does not yet publish together. Position is exposure against preparedness; the margin is their difference.

blocks.caption: Distribution of the current universe across the four quadrants, on median cut-lines (exposure ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, preparedness ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}).

blocks.text: The field is not uniformly exposed. {{fact:earning_count}} entities ({{fact:earning_pct}}) sit in Earning it and {{fact:sidelined_count}} ({{fact:sidelined_pct}}) in Sidelined — postures a damage-first stack would largely approve. Only {{fact:exposed_count}} ({{fact:exposed_pct}}) occupy Exposed: a non-firm bet running ahead of product, register fit and capital depth. That minority is structurally informative; it is where the connection agreement and the BI wording diverge, not where headline premium concentrates.

The margin spread is {{fact:mos_spread}} points against a median of {{fact:median_mos}} — wide enough that posture, not pedigree, separates the tails. At one end, {{fact:top_mos_name}} shows preparedness (capital, specialist product, data) currently outrunning the non-firm exposure on the book; at the other, {{fact:low_mos_name}} sits at {{fact:low_mos_val}} because exposure has outrun the means to carry it. The construct is not judging good or bad businesses. It is asking whether the bet and the balance sheet still match.

Whitespace is the commercial hinge: {{fact:whitespace_count}} entities ({{fact:whitespace_pct}}) sit high on preparedness, low on exposure — rated capital, specialist product and broker infrastructure the market has not yet routed onto availability risk. That is not a roster of winners; it is a structural surplus created when grid reform produces interruptible load faster than wordings produce triggers. {{fact:top_whitespace_name}} is representative: preparation on the balance sheet, negligible availability premium on the disclosed book — capacity waiting for a peril the schedule cannot yet name. The deployment question is who moves first from could write the cover to is writing it, before queue repricing closes the gap.{{cite:ACAD-CLARKE-INDEX-DEMAND,SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL}}

The peril does not distribute evenly across the value chain. Exposed concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}} — which is structurally right, because non-firm intensity is a register fact at Layer 3 before it propagates upward. Carriers and intermediaries appear more often in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) than in Exposed, because balance-sheet preparedness is easier to evidence than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside.

Layer 1 still contributes {{fact:exposed_l1}} Exposed names and Layer 2 contributes {{fact:exposed_l2}} — books where concentration outruns product fit — while Layer 4 shows {{fact:exposed_l4}} Exposed so far. With only {{fact:measured_pct}} measured share, the layer skew is more stable than rank order inside a quadrant; magnitudes at the asset layer will move as registers land even when the chain logic does not.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI}}
Assets and carriers running ahead of preparedness

Within Exposed, the deepest negative gap belongs to {{fact:worst_exposed_name}} — flexible-connection or concentrated energy exposure without a matching availability line on the file. {{fact:exposed_l3}} of {{fact:exposed_count}} Exposed names are assets, where curtailment rights in the connection agreement precede mitigation evidence in the tower. Of {{fact:l3_total}} scored campuses, {{fact:gate_firm_count}} carry firm Gate status in the register and {{fact:gate_unknown_count}} remain unknown; the index reports both and infers neither.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}}

The headline finding is not a ranking. It is that exposure and preparedness genuinely come apart — across {{fact:total}} entities and {{fact:mos_spread}} points of margin spread — which is the whole reason a one-axis hazard score would mislead, and a margin would not.
What would change, and what would not

Only {{fact:measured_pct}} of the score rests on measured evidence, so the index stays provisional and should be read as direction, not measurement. What moves as live data lands is the magnitude and ordering within each quadrant: as non-firm intensity is pulled from connection registers and capital from filings, entities will shift across the median cut-lines (currently exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}) and relative placement will firm up. What does not change is the construct — the two axes, the margin, and the finding that they separate. This section re-runs automatically on every build, against whatever the registers then say.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}}
